rulings: B20, 2026-10-14: MNIST pooled to 8 x 8; FC1 and FC2 the host's at 8 bits, trained with no tile noise; FC3 trained for the tile at 6 bits; all three in one run of grx930's harness; FC2 to FC3 by min((x + 2) >> 2, 31)
seed rule, 2026-10-14T21:39:28Z, before any canary network was trained: seed 1's network is the canary, seeds 2 to 5 reported beside it
2026-10-14T23:37:11Z: FC3's declared reference is the 8-bit converter's codes

2026-10-14T23:37:11Z: one output scale for FC3, fixed once at calibration on the calibration set and never on the acceptance vectors; Gate F reported with it and without, the band set on the figure with it

workload.acceptance_order: file order: the first 1,000 images of MNIST's test file
workload.intended_classes: the digits 0 to 9 on outputs 0 to 9; outputs 10 to 15 trained toward no class

dataset.name: MNIST, each image pooled to 8 x 8
dataset.license_and_usage_terms: CC BY-SA 3.0, copyright Yann LeCun and Corinna Cortes, as Keras's documentation states them
dataset.split_name: acceptance: test file, images 0 to 999; calibration: training file, images 54,000 to 54,999
dataset.sample_id_source: mnist-t10k-NNNNN and mnist-train-NNNNN, the image's index in its file
dataset.preprocessing: the middle 24 x 24 of each 28 x 28 image in 3 x 3 blocks, each block's mean (2s + 9) div 18; then (127p + 127) div 255

graph.format: int8 weights and operands, int32 sums; bias added; ReLU; (v + 2^8) >> 9, held at 127

graph.engine: PTA, 128 x 64 tile, one shot a vector
graph.format: 6-bit activation codes 0..31, 6-bit weight codes -32..31, exact sum s; the 8-bit converter's code floor(s / 32 + 1/2), held to -128..127, a held code a range fault
graph.class: the largest of code x 512 + bias, the lowest index on a tie

training.harness: grx930 c930/sim/pta_mnist.c, pta_tile_model.c and .h, pta_mnist.sh, built with -DN_SIDE=8 -DN_HID=64 -DN_OUT=16
training.build: gcc -O2 -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic, gcc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, glibc 2.39, on Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2 (kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2); the harness's arithmetic is integer, but for the double-precision logits, which are summed in a fixed order
training.start_network: pta_mnist train --din 8 --wbits 8 --seed 1 --hidden 2: din=8 wbits=8 seed=1 from=0 from_epochs=0 epochs=6 held_out=96.93 digital=96.08 hidden=2
training.canary_network: pta_mnist train --din 8 --wbits 6 --host 2 --seed 1 --hidden 2 --from h2_d8_b8_s1.net --sumnoise 0.1 --epochs 8: din=8 wbits=6 seed=1 from=8 from_epochs=6 epochs=8 held_out=97.52 digital=96.84 hidden=2 host=2 sumnoise=0.1 got=0.0000,0.0000,0.0999 fixed_epochs=8
training.seeds: the network's seed, 1; the training's shuffles and noise are drawn from it by the harness
training.checkpoint_selection_rule: the seed rule above; the training runs a fixed eight epochs
training.determinism: trained twice, byte for byte the same network; written twice, byte for byte the same tensors

generation.command: SHAPE=chain sim/pta_mnist.sh MNIST_GZ WORK canary; then SHAPE=chain sim/pta_mnist.sh MNIST_GZ WORK golden
generation.harness_line: golden: net_seed=1 net_wbits=6 net_host=2 images=1000 cal=1000 cal_first=54000 abits=6 adcbits=8 tile=128x64 sh=9,9 S=9 code_shift=5 clipped=0 tile_differ=0 of 32000 act_differ=0 of 256000 declared_right=96.60 highprec_right=96.80 highprec_agree=99.20

artifacts.role: the acceptance images pooled to 8 x 8, the network's training input over 255
the acceptance vectors as FC1 takes them: (127p + 127) div 255
the acceptance images' digits; for task quality, not the declared reference
the acceptance vectors' ids, in order
artifacts.dtype_encoding: UTF-8 text, one 'mnist-t10k-NNNNN' and LF a line

artifacts.role: FC1's weights
FC1's biases, in its sums' units, added before the ReLU
FC2's weights
FC2's biases, in its sums' units, added before the ReLU
FC3's weights trained for the tile, as 6-bit codes
FC3's biases, applied by the CPU to each code at its step, 2^9 of FC2-operand times weight-operand units
FC1's outputs after bias, ReLU, rescale and saturation
FC2's outputs, the same
FC3's activation codes: min((x + 2) >> 2, 31) of FC2's outputs
FC3's exact sums of activation code times weight code, before the converter
FC3's declared reference: the 8-bit converter's code of each sum
artifacts.dtype_encoding: int8, -128..127: floor(sum / 32 + 1/2), held, step 2^5 of the sums

artifacts.role: the class: the largest of code x 2^9 + bias, the lowest index on a tie
the network as trained, in double precision on the pixels over 255, no quantiser
the calibration set: the first 1,000 of the 6,000 held-out training images, as FC1 takes them
their digits
their ids, in order
artifacts.dtype_encoding: UTF-8 text, one 'mnist-train-NNNNN' and LF a line

artifacts.role: FC3's declared reference on them, against which one output scale is fixed
the canary, seed 1, as grx930's harness wrote it (PTAMLP4)
the 8-bit network of seed 1 the canary was trained from

gate_f.per_run_normalized_rms_percent: 100 * sqrt(sum((output - reference)^2) / sum(reference^2)) over 1,000 vectors x 16 outputs, in codes
gate_f.output_scale: one scale for FC3, the least-squares slope through the origin of calibration_fc3_reference on the PTA's codes over the calibration set, the PTA's codes times it; fixed once a calibration, never on the acceptance vectors
gate_f.status: the band, the tail rule and the class threshold are proposed from the frozen canary's model run and ruled by the freeze's owner

serialization.tensor_file_format: headerless raw bytes; shape, type and encoding as above
serialization.json_digest: SHA-256 of this file's canonical form: keys sorted, no whitespace, UTF-8; with no number but integers and no character past ASCII in it, that is RFC 8785's form (JCS)
